messages.author: 844883af0e01bd3e
messages.subject: Survival analysis WinBUGS vs Stan
parts:
Hi stan-users,

I'm a newcomer to Stan-type models, and I'm wondering how to implement survival models with censored data.
I have the following in WinBUGS

surt[i] ~ dweib(p,mut[i])I(surt.cen[i],)
log(mut[i]) <- beta2[1] + beta2[2]*gender[i] + beta2[3]*idade.int[i] + beta2[4]*prevoi[i]


how can I implement it in Stan?


Thank's

messages.author: 844883af0e01bd3e
messages.subject: Re: Survival analysis WinBUGS vs Stan
parts:
Ok,

I solved the question

https://github.com/stan-dev/stan/blob/master/src/models/bugs_examples/vol1/kidney/kidney.stan

Thanks

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Survival analysis WinBUGS vs Stan
parts: The kidney example is not the greatest. Other resources include: Section 9.2 of the Stan manual discusses censoring, the Weibull log-likelihood can be found in the index, appendix C discusses the most important differences between BUGS and Stan models.
